title: Device sender characterization and remaining HSV kernels

method.input: Precomputed float64 RGB; fixed random seed 2058; dense alternation, sparse max(1,floor(pixels/100)) changes, static frames
method.sender_scope: Real flush, synchronous library serialization and intercepted transport; discovery/authentication/periodic SDK threads excluded
method.encode_mode: Counting sink; does not simulate wire capacity
method.loopback_mode: Real UDP/TCP on 127.0.0.2, separate validating receiver process; sender CPU excludes receiver
method.timing: Per-flush and per-write instrumentation included. Receiver backpressure and scheduling can affect loopback rates. Preflight/seed delivery is outside measured interval.
method.catalog: 3 repeats x 0.7 s at 60/300/1000 pixels; screening duration, not universal capacity claims
method.large: 3 repeats x 2 s at 10000/500000 pixels, unpaced; explicit skips for format/packet-count limits
method.paced: 3 repeats x 2 s, target 60 flushes/s; missed timing is not hidden by queuing
method.traffic: 3 repeats x 1.2 s, static/sparse; partial DNRGB keepalives are not counted as complete frames
method.effects: 3 repeats x 8 s + 2 s warmup, 500000 pixels, synthetic audio, standard asyncio, full websocket and loopback DDP; effect harness retains its original 127.0.0.1 route in both before/after
method.profiling: Separate 3 s CPU sampling per sender family and 5 s per affected effect. Sender shares filter measure_flushes; effect shares filter active render/audio/preview stacks. No profiled timings used for speedup claims.
method.data_state: Raw metadata records revision and dirty status; some measurements preceded their equivalent code commit. Original invalid Art-Net measurements are retained and replaced by repaired runs in final comparison tables.

findings: Art-Net validation found the library simplified-mode setter clamps universe addresses above 255. Default RGB/510-channel layouts therefore break above 43520 pixels. The fix selects explicit Net/Sub-Net/Universe addressing, rebuilds the header once per packet, and rejects addresses/layouts beyond universe 32767. Eight regression cases cover valid address boundaries and invalid output layouts; the original regression run failed five cases before the fix. The legacy config schema is unchanged.

OPC originally spent 99.47% of measured encoding samples in its per-pixel send_out loop. Vectorized clipping/casting preserves scalar RGB bytes for common numeric types and strided inputs, rejects malformed shapes and preserves NaN/inf errors before transmission.
DDP loopback CPU is largely socket writing (85.50% at Sink.send, including benchmark transport/counters). Sender-only results omit effect rendering and websocket costs.

E131 encoding samples: 44.46% in LedFx flush, 22.56% in the library DMX validation generator, 20.98% in the library DMX setter. Array/list/tuple conversion and validation are the next strong candidate, rather than an event-loop change.
OSC per-address modes create one or three messages per pixel; all-to-one reduces message count but creates large single UDP datagrams with a hard size limit.
DNRGB uses partial static keepalive traffic; the benchmark seeds a full image before sparse/static measurements and records partial refreshes separately.

Melt & Sparkle caches a pixel-count-only initial wave and reuses frame buffers; the extra persistent cache costs 8 bytes/pixel (about 3.8 MiB at 500000 pixels). HSV gradient gathers now write directly into the output buffer. Crawler effect time improves, but its render FPS ranges overlap; no clear throughput claim for Crawler.

OpenRGB currently uses one TCP send call, not sendall. These measurements observed no short writes; the harness rejects short writes or trailing incomplete TCP messages. Congested links are not covered.

serial_example.note: Theoretical transport ceiling only; encoding measurements exclude physical serial transmission and controller/display time.

limitations: Single-host synthetic tests, not device firmware/Wi-Fi/physical LED latency or all configurations.
Application bytes exclude UDP/IP/Ethernet overhead. TCP writes and parsed messages are not network packet counts.
Protocols lacking a frame ID support matching ordered packet sets, not proof of atomic hardware display updates.
Serial/Hue cover encoding only. LIFX, Twinkly, Zengge, Launchpad and Raspberry Pi require additional SDK/hardware fixtures; WLED delegates to measured senders.
Python 3.15 remains experimental; project Python support metadata is unchanged.
Sequential repeated runs, not randomized trials; raw results and min/max ranges are retained.

validation.numeric_and_protocol_checks: Byte-level decoding, scalar RGB equivalence, missing/mixed DDP packets, partial keepalives, TCP short-write detection, Art-Net addressing boundaries, profile-scope isolation
validation.pyrefly: zero new errors; five old suppressions removed
validation.schema_compatibility: Frozen legacy and model schemas preserved; full Art-Net channel span checked during output setup.

reproduce: Repeat selected senders with --fps 60 --modes loopback for paced CPU/delivery, or --patterns sparse,static --seconds 1.2 for traffic suppression.

For the affected HSV profile sweep use --effects blade_power_plus,block_reflections,crawler,energy2,fire,glitch,lava_lamp,marching,melt,melt_and_sparkle,water --sampling cpu --seconds 5 --repeats 1, then tools/effect_profile_report.py.
